real_conflicts: The proposal to 'remove individual rounded card containers' (Unity/Consistency) risks making the genre text even harder to read. Currently, the cards provide a dark background that boosts contrast for the small genre text; removing them against the dark background pattern will likely render the genre information invisible, violating the requirement for visible detail.

The proposal to 'consolidate the layout into a single, unified timeline' (Simplicity/Legibility) creates a severe density conflict. Compressing three simultaneous stages into one vertical column will force the text to become microscopic or the page to become excessively long, destroying the 'single-page' constraint and making the schedule impossible to scan quickly.
accepted: The proposal to 'introduce a distinct visual accent (colored left-border stroke)' (Variety/Distinctiveness) is accepted. This adds information density (visual cues for genre) without consuming valuable horizontal space or cluttering the grid.
concession: I concede that the current 'floating card' aesthetic is visually noisy. I agree to reduce the visual weight of the card borders and backgrounds, provided the text legibility is maintained.
compromise: We will retain the three-column grid to preserve the single-page format and chronological clarity. We will keep the card containers but strip them of heavy borders, using the 'colored left-border stroke' from the Variety proposal to define the cards. This ensures the genre text remains legible against a dark background while adding the requested energetic visual rhythm.
nonnegotiable: The canvas must be extended vertically to fully reveal the 7:00 PM headliner row and the footer information. No critical logistical data (venue, ticket info) may be truncated or hidden by low contrast.
